title: Heat Exhaustion & Heat Stroke
summary: Heat exhaustion: rest somewhere cool and drink. Heat stroke (confused, very hot) is life-threatening: call for help and cool them aggressively and immediately.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for possible heat stroke
when: Confusion, strange behaviour, slurred speech, seizure or collapse in the heat
Very high body temperature with hot skin (may be dry or sweaty)
Heat exhaustion that does not improve within 30 minutes, or vomiting so they cannot drink

steps.title: Move them somewhere cool
steps.text: Into shade or air conditioning. Remove excess clothing and protective equipment.

steps.title: Heat exhaustion (alert, sweating, tired, headache, nausea)
steps.text: Have them lie down and drink cool fluids – an electrolyte or sports drink is ideal, water if not. Cool the skin with water and fanning.

steps.title: Heat stroke: cool immediately
steps.text: If they are confused or collapsed, call {EMERGENCY} and start cooling at once. The best method is immersing the body up to the neck in cold water.
points: If immersion is not possible: soak them with cold water, fan continuously, and apply cold packs or ice wrapped in cloth to the neck, armpits and groin
Keep cooling until help arrives or they become fully alert

steps.title: Monitor
steps.text: Check breathing and response. Recovery position if unresponsive and breathing; CPR if not breathing normally.

warningSigns: Hot skin with very high temperature
doNot: Do not give fluids to someone who is confused or cannot swallow safely
Do not delay cooling to transport them – start cooling first
Do not give medicines such as paracetamol/acetaminophen or aspirin for heat stroke
